task_3.title: Dataset.update() now returns None instead of Self
task_3.description: Dataset.update() completes its long-standing deprecation cycle (started in v0.17, originally scheduled for v0.21) by changing its return type from Self to None. The method continues to mutate the dataset in-place, but callers that relied on the returned reference (e.g., for method chaining or assignment) will now receive None, which can cause AttributeError or silent logic bugs at runtime.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset.update() no longer returns the dataset instance and instead returns None, completing the deprecation of its return value. Any existing code that captures or chains on the return value of Dataset.update() must be updated to treat the call as a purely in-place mutation with no usable return value.

expectation.grounded: Dataset.update(other: CoercibleMapping) must have return type None. Calling Dataset.update() must still apply the in-place merge via the internal _replace mechanism, but the method must not return Self. The 'Returns' section of the docstring must be removed. The type annotation must reflect -> None.
expectation.conceptual: Dataset.update() should behave like dict.update(): it mutates the dataset in-place and returns None. Users who previously captured the return value for chaining or assignment should instead call update() as a standalone statement and reference the original dataset variable for subsequent operations.

constraints.grounded: The in-place mutation behavior of Dataset.update() must remain identical — all variable merging logic via dataset_update_method and _replace(inplace=True) must continue to function correctly. No other Dataset methods (e.g., merge, assign) should be affected by this change. The method must still raise ValueError for incompatible variable conflicts.
constraints.conceptual: Only the return value contract changes; the mutation semantics and variable-merging behavior of update() must be fully preserved. No other public API methods on Dataset should change behavior as a side effect of this modification.

Code that assigns the return value (e.g., result = ds.update(other)) will bind result to None.

task_5.title: Hide empty sections in HTML reprs and auto-expand DataTree sub-groups
task_5.description: The HTML representations for DataArray, Dataset, and DataTree now hide empty sections (coordinates, indexes, attributes) instead of rendering them as blank collapsible panels. This makes the HTML repr consistent with the text repr. Additionally, the DataTree HTML repr automatically expands sub-groups when a group level has no data variables, making it easier to visualize nested DataTree structures. DataArray name rendering now uses proper HTML escaping, and DataTree child nodes are rendered with semantic CSS classes instead of inline styles.

task_1.title: Extend DataTree.from_dict() to accept DataArray values, coords, and nested dicts
task_1.description: DataTree.from_dict() is enhanced to accept a broader range of input types beyond just Dataset and DataTree objects. Users can now pass DataArray-coercible values (tuples, arrays, scalars, etc.) as dict values, which are automatically grouped by parent path and assembled into Dataset nodes. A new 'coords' parameter allows specifying coordinate variables separately from data variables, mirroring the Dataset constructor's data/coords distinction. Additionally, when nested=True is passed, nested Python dictionaries are recursively flattened into path-keyed entries, eliminating the need for manual pre-flattening. The first positional parameter is renamed from 'd' to 'data'.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that DataTree.from_dict() supports constructing a DataTree from DataArray-coercible values (not only Dataset/DataTree objects), supports a 'coords' parameter for specifying coordinate variables at arbitrary tree paths, and supports automatic flattening of nested dictionaries when nested=True is specified. Ensure the previous positional-only parameter 'd' is renamed to 'data' and is no longer positional-only.

expectation.grounded: DataTree.from_dict() accepts a 'data' mapping whose values may be Dataset, DataTree, None, or any object coercible into a DataArray (matching the FromDictDataValue type alias). A new 'coords' keyword parameter accepts a mapping of path-keyed CoercibleValue objects that become coordinate variables on the corresponding parent Dataset nodes. A new keyword-only 'nested' parameter (default False) controls whether dict-typed values in 'data' and 'coords' are recursively flattened into slash-separated path keys. When nested=False and a dict value is encountered in 'data' or 'coords', a TypeError is raised. DataArray-coercible values at leaf paths are grouped by their parent NodePath and assembled into a Dataset via the Dataset constructor; if construction fails, the original ValueError or TypeError is re-raised with a message identifying the failing node path. Overloaded type signatures distinguish the nested=True and nested=False cases for static type checking. NodePath.absolute() is used to canonicalize all keys to absolute paths, and duplicate paths raise a ValueError.
expectation.conceptual: DataTree.from_dict() accepts DataArray-like values in addition to Dataset and DataTree objects. A separate 'coords' argument allows coordinate variables to be specified independently from data variables at any tree path. Nested Python dictionaries can be passed directly and are auto-flattened when nested=True is set. The method validates that no duplicate paths exist after canonicalization, that DataArray values are not placed at the root, and that DataArray values do not conflict with explicitly set parent nodes.

constraints.grounded: Passing Dataset, DataTree, or None values in the 'data' mapping must continue to work as before. Root node data specified via '', '.', '/', or './' path keys must still be handled correctly. Child nodes must still be inserted in depth-first order (sorted by path depth) to satisfy tree construction ordering (GH issue #9276). When nested=False (the default), nested dict values must raise TypeError, preserving backward compatibility with the original flat-dict-only interface. The 'coords' values must not appear as data variables and vice versa. Attempting to set a DataArray value at the root path must raise ValueError. Attempting to set a DataArray value at a path whose parent is also explicitly set must raise ValueError.
constraints.conceptual: Existing usage patterns with flat dictionaries of Dataset and DataTree values must remain fully backward-compatible. The default behavior (nested=False) must not accept nested dicts to avoid ambiguity with existing type signatures. Coordinate and data variable namespaces must remain distinct. The tree construction order must be preserved to avoid parent-before-child insertion errors.

task_6.title: Default Zarr fill_value to NaN for float variables in Zarr v3
task_6.description: In Zarr v2, Xarray conflated _FillValue and fill_value, so unwritten float data in Zarr stores was decoded as NaN. With Zarr v3, unwritten data instead used Zarr's default fill_value of 0, causing silent data corruption where missing or unwritten float chunks appeared as zeros rather than NaN. This change makes Zarr v3 float variables consistently default to a fill_value of NaN, matching the long-standing Zarr v2 behavior. Non-float dtypes continue to use Zarr's default fill_value of zero. Users can override the fill_value via the encoding parameter in to_zarr().

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when writing Zarr v3 stores via Xarray, unwritten or lazily-computed float variable chunks default to a fill_value of NaN instead of zero. Previously, writing Zarr metadata with compute=False and then reading back the store would decode unwritten float data as all zeros under Zarr v3, while Zarr v2 correctly decoded them as NaN. This inconsistency caused silent data corruption for workflows relying on NaN to indicate missing or not-yet-written data.

expectation.grounded: When ZarrStore serializes a floating-point variable (dtype.kind == 'f') to Zarr v3 format and no explicit fill_value is provided in encoding, the store must set fill_value to NaN. For Zarr v2 format, existing behavior where _FillValue drives the fill value is unchanged. For non-float dtypes, the Zarr default fill_value of zero continues to apply. Users may override this default by passing a fill_value in the encoding dict to Dataset.to_zarr() or DataArray.to_zarr().
expectation.conceptual: When writing float variables to a Zarr store without an explicit fill_value, the library should default to NaN as the fill value for unwritten chunks, regardless of whether Zarr v2 or v3 format is used. Non-float variables should continue to use zero as the default fill value. Users should be able to override the default fill_value through the encoding parameter.

constraints.grounded: The NaN default must only apply to floating-point dtypes (dtype.kind == 'f') under Zarr v3 code paths. Zarr v2 fill_value handling via _FillValue must remain unchanged. If a user explicitly provides a fill_value in encoding (including zero), the explicit value must take precedence over the NaN default. Non-float dtypes must not be affected by this change.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not alter behavior for integer or other non-float types. Explicit user-provided fill values must always take precedence over the new default. Zarr v2 write behavior must remain unchanged to avoid regressions.

task_7.title: Restore pickle support for h5netcdf-backed datasets opened from file-like objects
task_7.description: A regression introduced between 2025.7.1 and 2025.8.0 caused h5netcdf-backed xarray datasets opened from file-like objects (e.g., via s3fs or other remote filesystems) to fail when pickled, raising a TypeError from h5py. This broke cloudpickle-based workflows including Dask parallelism over remote datasets. The fix introduces a new PickleableFileManager that stores the opener callable and its arguments, enabling files to be reopened upon unpickling. H5NetCDFStore now routes file-like objects and remote URIs through PickleableFileManager instead of using a raw file handle or CachingFileManager, restoring pickle round-trip support.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray datasets opened via `xr.open_dataset()` with `engine='h5netcdf'` from file-like objects (e.g., objects returned by `s3fs.S3FileSystem.open()`) can be successfully pickled and unpickled using cloudpickle or the standard pickle module. Previously, attempting to pickle such datasets raised `TypeError: h5py objects cannot be pickled`, breaking Dask-based parallel workflows over remote netCDF files.

expectation.grounded: When a dataset is opened via `xr.open_dataset()` with `engine='h5netcdf'` from a file-like object or remote URI, the resulting Dataset and its underlying file manager must support `__getstate__` and `__setstate__` for pickle round-tripping. The file manager used for non-local-path sources is `PickleableFileManager`, which stores the opener callable (`h5netcdf.File`), positional args, mode, and keyword args. On unpickle, `PickleableFileManager.__setstate__` reinvokes the opener to reopen the file. Write mode 'w' is converted to 'a' before storage to prevent data loss on reopen. `CachingFileManager` is only used when the filename is a local string path (i.e., `isinstance(filename, str)` and not a remote URI). Pickling a closed `PickleableFileManager` results in a closed manager upon unpickling.
expectation.conceptual: Datasets backed by h5netcdf and opened from file-like objects or remote URIs must survive a pickle round-trip without raising errors. After unpickling, the dataset must be fully functional with data accessible as before. The system must distinguish between local file paths (which use cached file management) and file-like objects or remote URIs (which use pickle-safe file management). Pickling a dataset whose file has already been closed should produce a closed dataset on unpickle rather than an error.

constraints.grounded: Datasets opened from local string file paths via `engine='h5netcdf'` must continue to use `CachingFileManager` with its global caching and locking behavior. The `PickleableFileManager` must not break the `FileManager` interface contract: `acquire()`, `acquire_context()`, and `close()` must behave consistently. The pickle state must not retain a reference to the open file object itself. The opener callable and its arguments must themselves be pickleable for the round-trip to succeed. The `_remove_del_methods` atexit handler must cover both `CachingFileManager` and `PickleableFileManager` to avoid errors during interpreter shutdown.
constraints.conceptual: Existing behavior for locally-opened h5netcdf datasets must not regress. The file management interface must remain consistent regardless of which manager implementation is used. Pickle support depends on the underlying file-like object's opener being pickleable; if it is not, the limitation is documented rather than silently failing. Resources must be properly cleaned up on close, and closed managers must not allow further data access.

task_4.title: Change default netCDF engine preference order and add netcdf_engine_order option
task_4.description: The default engine used when reading and writing netCDF files has changed from preferring netcdf4-python to preferring h5netcdf and scipy, which are typically faster and more concurrency-friendly. The new default engine preference order is h5netcdf > scipy > netcdf4, replacing the prior order of netcdf4 > h5netcdf > scipy. A new netcdf_engine_order parameter in set_options() allows users to customize this preference order or restore the previous defaults. The hardcoded NETCDF_BACKENDS_ORDER constant has been replaced by the dynamic, user-configurable option. Additionally, the write-side engine selection function now accepts the file path directly and handles NCZarr mode paths, and the open_datatree/open_groups engine guessing now filters for backends that support groups.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the default netCDF engine preference order is changed from netcdf4 > h5netcdf > scipy to h5netcdf > scipy > netcdf4 for both reading and writing operations. Ensure that a new set_options() parameter named netcdf_engine_order is available to let users customize the engine preference order. Ensure that users who depend on the prior default behavior can restore it by setting netcdf_engine_order to ['netcdf4', 'h5netcdf', 'scipy']. Ensure that open_datatree and open_groups only auto-select engines that support hierarchical groups.

expectation.grounded: When no engine is explicitly specified, open_dataset(), open_dataarray(), open_datatree(), open_groups(), open_mfdataset(), Dataset.to_netcdf(), DataArray.to_netcdf(), DataTree.to_netcdf(), and save_mfdataset() should select the first available engine from the netcdf_engine_order option (default: h5netcdf, scipy, netcdf4). The set_options() function should accept a netcdf_engine_order parameter whose value is any permutation or subset of ['h5netcdf', 'scipy', 'netcdf4']. The sort_backends() function should use the dynamic netcdf_engine_order option instead of a hardcoded constant. The get_default_netcdf_write_engine() function should consult OPTIONS['netcdf_engine_order'] and should handle NCZarr mode paths by forcing netcdf4, exclude netcdf4 for IOBase targets, exclude h5netcdf for NETCDF3 formats, and exclude scipy for non-NETCDF3 formats. For open_datatree and open_groups, guess_engine() should be called with must_support_groups=True to filter out backends that lack group support (e.g., scipy). An invalid netcdf_engine_order value should raise ValueError.
expectation.conceptual: When users read or write netCDF files without specifying an engine, the library should default to h5netcdf first, then scipy, then netcdf4, selecting the first one that is installed and compatible with the requested format and target. Users should be able to override this preference order globally via set_options(). When opening hierarchical data (DataTree or groups), the engine auto-selection should only consider backends capable of reading groups. The previous behavior can be fully restored via a single set_options() call.

constraints.grounded: The netcdf_engine_order option must only accept values that are subsets of {'h5netcdf', 'scipy', 'netcdf4'}; other values must trigger a validation error. Existing explicit engine= parameters on all I/O functions must continue to override the default order. Format-based engine filtering must remain intact: h5netcdf must be excluded for NETCDF3 formats, scipy must be excluded for NETCDF4 formats, and netcdf4 must be forced for NCZarr mode paths. The option must be usable as a context manager via set_options(). When no suitable engine from the configured order is installed, a ValueError must be raised explaining which libraries are needed.
constraints.conceptual: The engine preference order must be globally configurable without breaking explicit engine selections. Format-specific engine constraints must still be enforced regardless of the configured order. The configuration must be validated at set-time, not at use-time. Backward compatibility must be achievable through the new configuration option.

task_8.title: Scipy backend no longer closes underlying file-like objects on close
task_8.description: When Xarray objects were opened from file-like objects using engine='scipy', closing the Xarray object would incorrectly close the underlying file-like object as well. This was caused by scipy.io.netcdf_file's close() method unconditionally closing file objects passed to its constructor (scipy issue #13905). The fix introduces a subclass that overrides close() to only flush and reset the file position, leaving the underlying file open. This aligns the scipy backend's behavior with the h5netcdf backend, which already preserved the underlying file on close.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that closing an Xarray Dataset or DataArray opened from a file-like object (e.g., BytesIO) with engine='scipy' does not close the underlying file-like object. Previously, the scipy backend would close the caller-supplied file handle when the Xarray object was closed, preventing subsequent reads or reuse of that file object. This was inconsistent with the h5netcdf backend, which correctly left the underlying file open.

expectation.grounded: When a ScipyDataStore is constructed from a file-like object (any object with a seek method), the internal netcdf dataset should use a flush_only_netcdf_file subclass of scipy.io.netcdf_file. Calling close() on that dataset must flush buffered data and reset the file position via seek(0), but must not close the underlying file object. The __del__ destructor must not trigger a close of the file. The DummyFileManager wrapping the dataset should use the default close behavior (delegating to the subclass's overridden close) rather than a custom flush-only close callback.
expectation.conceptual: When a user opens an Xarray object from a file-like object using the scipy engine and subsequently closes the Xarray object, the underlying file-like object must remain open and seeked to position zero, ready for further reads. The close operation should flush any pending writes but must not invalidate or close the file handle. This behavior must be consistent with how the h5netcdf backend handles the same scenario.

constraints.grounded: The flush_only_netcdf_file subclass must only be used when the input is a file-like object (detected via the presence of a seek attribute), not when a file path string is provided. The mmap assertion (use_mmap is False) must continue to hold for file-like objects. The standard scipy.io.netcdf_file class must still be used for regular file path inputs. Gzip-compressed file path handling must remain unaffected when flush_only is False.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must only change close behavior for file-like object inputs, not for file path inputs. Memory-mapped file access must remain unsupported for file-like objects. Normal file-path-based opens must continue to use the standard scipy netcdf_file behavior. Compressed (.gz) file handling must remain unchanged.

task_2.title: Support in-memory netCDF reads and writes with engine='netcdf4'
task_2.description: The netCDF4 backend now supports reading from bytes/memoryview and writing to in-memory buffers, bringing it to parity with the scipy and h5netcdf backends. This includes DataTree support, a new PickleableFileManager for pickling in-memory datasets, refactoring of write functions into a dedicated writers module, and updated engine selection logic. All netCDF backends now support in-memory reads and writes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the netCDF4 backend (`engine='netcdf4'`) supports reading netCDF data from in-memory `bytes` or `memoryview` objects and writing netCDF data to in-memory buffers (returning a `memoryview`), for both `Dataset` and `DataTree`. Previously, the netCDF4 engine only supported file-path-based I/O, while scipy and h5netcdf already supported in-memory operations. Ensure that xarray objects opened from in-memory bytes with `engine='netcdf4'` can be pickled. Ensure that `NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open` correctly identifies in-memory `bytes`/`memoryview` containing valid netCDF data. Ensure that the default write engine selection accounts for in-memory targets appropriately via the configurable `netcdf_engine_order` option.

expectation.grounded: When `Dataset.to_netcdf()` or `DataTree.to_netcdf()` is called with `path_or_file=None` and `engine='netcdf4'`, the method should return a `memoryview` containing valid netCDF4 data. The `get_default_netcdf_write_engine()` function should use `OPTIONS['netcdf_engine_order']` for engine preference ordering and should only exclude `netcdf4` from candidates when the target is an `IOBase` file object, not for `bytes`/`memoryview`/`None` targets.
expectation.conceptual: All xarray netCDF backends (netcdf4, scipy, h5netcdf) should uniformly support reading from in-memory byte data and writing to in-memory buffers. In-memory datasets should be pickleable, enabling use with distributed computing frameworks. The engine auto-selection logic should respect user-configurable engine ordering preferences and correctly distinguish in-memory targets from file-object targets.

constraints.grounded: Existing file-path-based I/O with `engine='netcdf4'` must continue to work identically. `CachingFileManager` should still be used for file-path-based opens; `PickleableFileManager` is only for in-memory (bytes/memoryview) opens with netCDF4. `DummyFileManager` is used for in-memory writes with netCDF4. The `to_netcdf()` return type contract must be preserved: `memoryview` when `path_or_file=None`, `None` when writing to a path with `compute=True`, `Delayed` when `compute=False`. Write locking (`get_write_lock`) must only be combined when the filename is a string path, not for in-memory targets. The `FileManager` class hierarchy must remain generic and backward-compatible for all existing backends.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not regress any existing netCDF I/O workflows, including file-based reads/writes, multifile datasets, remote URI access, dask-backed lazy writes, or pickling of file-based datasets. The in-memory feature must integrate seamlessly with the existing engine selection, encoding validation, and unlimited dimensions handling. Lock semantics must remain correct for concurrent access patterns.

task_9.title: Fix align_chunks parameter not passed in Dataset.to_zarr()
task_9.description: The align_chunks parameter on Dataset.to_zarr() was not being forwarded to the underlying backend API call, rendering the automatic chunk alignment feature non-functional for Dataset objects (it only worked for DataArray). This could lead to silent data loss or corruption when appending chunked data to Zarr stores in parallel Dask contexts. The fix also handles an edge case where Zarr chunk sizes exceed the variable size, uses the variable shape directly for grid chunk computation instead of summing Dask chunk sizes, and improves the chunk misalignment error message to report which chunks overlap and on which axis.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the align_chunks parameter on Dataset.to_zarr() is correctly forwarded to the backend so that automatic chunk alignment works for Dataset objects, not just DataArray objects. Ensure that chunk alignment handles the edge case where Zarr encoding chunk sizes are larger than the variable's dimension size. Ensure that the chunk misalignment error message clearly identifies which Dask chunks overlap on the same Zarr chunk and on which axis.

expectation.grounded: When Dataset.to_zarr() is called with align_chunks=True, the align_chunks parameter must be propagated to the internal store write path (the same path used by DataArray.to_zarr()). The build_grid_chunks function must return early with the actual variable size when the Zarr chunk size is greater than or equal to the variable dimension size. The grid_rechunk function must compute grid chunks using the variable's shape rather than summing Dask chunk tuples. When validate_grid_chunks_alignment raises a ValueError for overlapping chunks, the error message must identify both the overlapping Dask chunk positions and the axis on which the overlap occurs.
expectation.conceptual: When a user writes a Dataset to Zarr with automatic chunk alignment enabled, the alignment must actually take effect, preventing silent data corruption during parallel writes. When the Zarr target chunk size exceeds the variable's dimension length, chunk computation must gracefully handle the mismatch without producing invalid chunk specifications. Chunk validation error messages must be actionable by clearly describing which chunks conflict and on which axis.

constraints.grounded: All existing Dataset.to_zarr() and DataArray.to_zarr() behavior with safe_chunks, region, append_dim, and write_empty_chunks parameters must remain unchanged. The align_nd_chunks function must continue to raise ValueError when backend and variable dimension counts or element counts differ. The validate_grid_chunks_alignment function must continue to raise ValueError for genuinely misaligned chunks. No changes to the public API signature of to_zarr().
constraints.conceptual: Existing Zarr write workflows that do not use align_chunks must not be affected. Chunk safety validation must remain intact and must not produce false negatives. The fix must not alter the public method signatures or introduce new required parameters.

task_11.title: Propagate coordinate attributes in Dataset.map() when keep_attrs=True
task_11.description: Dataset.map() was not preserving coordinate attributes when keep_attrs=True. When users performed operations that internally rely on Dataset.map() (such as weighted mean, weighted sum, and other weighted operations), coordinate metadata like standard_name, long_name, and units were silently dropped from all remaining coordinates in the result, even though keep_attrs=True was specified. The fix ensures that coordinate attributes are propagated in the same manner as data variable attributes, by copying original coordinate attrs back onto the resulting coordinates after the map function is applied.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset.map() preserves coordinate attributes when keep_attrs=True. Previously, calling Dataset.map() (or operations that depend on it, such as weighted mean/sum via the Weighted API) with keep_attrs=True would correctly preserve data variable attributes but silently discard all coordinate attributes. After any such operation, surviving coordinates would have empty attrs dictionaries, losing metadata such as standard_name, long_name, units, and axis. This must be fixed so that coordinate attrs are propagated consistently with data variable attrs.

expectation.grounded: When Dataset.map() is called with keep_attrs=True, the method must merge coordinates from the mapped result variables, construct a Coordinates object from the merged coordinate variables and indexes, and copy attrs from the original Dataset's coordinates onto the result coordinates. The resulting Dataset must be constructed with the explicit coords parameter so that coordinate attributes are retained. This also affects all operations that route through Dataset.map(), including Weighted.mean(), Weighted.sum(), and other weighted reduction methods. Coordinates present in both the source and result Datasets must have their attrs preserved; coordinates not present in the source are left unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: When a user performs any Dataset operation that maps a function over data variables (including weighted reductions like weighted mean) with keep_attrs=True, the resulting Dataset must retain the original attributes on all surviving coordinates. Coordinate metadata such as standard_name, long_name, units, and axis must not be lost.

constraints.grounded: When keep_attrs is False or unset, coordinate attributes must not be propagated (existing behavior unchanged). The attrs-copying semantics for coordinates must match the existing semantics for data variables: when keep_attrs=True, original attrs overwrite any changes made by the mapped function. Only coordinates that exist in the original Dataset should have their attrs copied; new coordinates introduced by the mapped function must retain whatever attrs they have. The coordinate merging must use merge_coordinates_without_align to properly handle indexes across the mapped data variables.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not change behavior when keep_attrs is False. Attribute propagation for coordinates must follow the same overwrite semantics already established for data variables. The change must not alter coordinate values or indexes, only their metadata attributes. Existing tests for Dataset.map() and weighted operations must continue to pass.

task_10.title: Fix encoding of empty numpy.datetime64 arrays with standard/gregorian calendar
task_10.description: Saving a Dataset containing a zero-length numpy.datetime64 variable with calendar encoding set to 'standard' or 'gregorian' raised a ValueError because np.nanmin was called on an empty array during the proleptic-Gregorian calendar check. The fix adds an early size check so that empty datetime arrays bypass the minimum-date comparison and encode successfully, consistent with the behavior when no calendar encoding is specified or when the array is non-empty.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that encoding an empty numpy.datetime64 array with a 'standard' or 'gregorian' calendar encoding does not raise a ValueError. Previously, calling Dataset.to_netcdf on a dataset with a zero-length datetime64 coordinate and calendar set to 'standard' failed with 'zero-size array to reduction operation fmin which has no identity', while the same operation succeeded for non-empty arrays or when no calendar encoding was specified.

expectation.grounded: When _eagerly_encode_cf_datetime receives dates with size 0 and the calendar is 'standard' or 'gregorian', it must skip the np.nanmin-based proleptic Gregorian mismatch check and proceed to encode successfully. The encode_cf_datetime function should return a valid encoded result (empty numeric array, units, calendar) without raising ValueError or OutOfBoundsDatetime. The DatetimeAccessor.encode method and downstream cf_encoder pipeline must complete without error.
expectation.conceptual: Encoding a zero-length datetime64 variable with any supported calendar, including 'standard' and 'gregorian', must succeed and produce a valid empty encoded output. The encoding path should handle empty arrays gracefully without attempting reduction operations that require at least one element.

constraints.grounded: The proleptic Gregorian / standard calendar mismatch detection (raising an error for dates before 1582-10-15) must still trigger for non-empty arrays whose minimum date predates the Gregorian reform. Non-empty datetime64 arrays must continue to be encoded identically to before the fix. The size guard must only skip the nanmin comparison, not bypass the rest of the encoding pipeline.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter the encoding behavior or validation logic for non-empty datetime arrays. Calendar mismatch detection for pre-Gregorian dates must remain intact. Only the empty-array edge case should be affected.

task_13.title: Propagate coordinate attributes in Dataset.map()
task_13.description: When calling Dataset.map() with keep_attrs=True, coordinate attributes were silently dropped from the result. synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset.map() preserves coordinate attributes when keep_attrs=True. task_14.title: Fix combine_attrs='drop_conflicts' for non-bool __eq__ results
task_14.description: When using combine_attrs='drop_conflicts' in xarray merge operations, attribute values whose __eq__ methods return non-boolean results (e.g., numpy arrays, Datasets, or other custom objects) would cause a ValueError due to ambiguous truth value evaluation. This fix makes the equivalence comparison robust against non-boolean equality results and uncatchable comparison exceptions, allowing drop_conflicts to gracefully treat incomparable attributes as conflicting rather than crashing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that combine_attrs='drop_conflicts' does not raise a ValueError when merging attributes whose values have __eq__ methods that return non-boolean results (e.g., numpy arrays). When two attribute values cannot be meaningfully compared for equality, they should be treated as conflicting and the attribute should be dropped, rather than the operation failing with an exception.

expectation.grounded: The `equivalent()` utility function must return a bool in all cases, including when the `==` operator on the compared objects returns a non-boolean type (e.g., numpy ndarray, pandas Series, xarray Dataset). It must accept `np.bool_` scalar results as valid booleans. It must still correctly detect NaN-equivalence for scalar NaN values. A new `equivalent_attrs()` function in the merge module must wrap `equivalent()` and catch `ValueError` and `TypeError` exceptions, returning `False` when comparisons are truly ambiguous. The `merge_attrs` function's `drop_conflicts` branch must use `equivalent_attrs()` for attribute comparisons.
expectation.conceptual: Attribute equivalence checks during merge operations must never raise exceptions due to non-standard equality implementations on attribute values. When two attribute values cannot be compared (because equality returns a non-boolean or raises an exception), they should be treated as non-equivalent, causing the attribute to be dropped under the drop_conflicts policy.

constraints.grounded: The `equivalent()` function must continue to delegate to `duck_array_ops.array_equiv` for ndarray inputs and to `list_equiv` for list inputs. NaN-equivalence for scalar values must be preserved. The `np.bool_` type must be accepted and converted to native Python bool. Non-boolean, non-np.bool_ comparison results must cause `equivalent()` to return `False` rather than raising. The `merge_attrs` function must not regress for combine_attrs modes other than 'drop_conflicts' (e.g., 'identical', 'no_conflicts', 'override', 'drop').
constraints.conceptual: Existing equivalence semantics for arrays, lists, and NaN values must be preserved. Only the handling of non-standard equality results is changed. task_15.title: Fix and expand Zarr encoding documentation for V2/V3 format differences
task_15.description: The Zarr encoding documentation contained incorrect example output and lacked coverage of how dimension and coordinate encoding differs between Zarr V2 and V3 formats. synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the Zarr encoding specification documentation accurately reflects the observable behavior of Zarr V2 and V3 formats. The previous documentation showed incorrect example output (suggesting _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS would appear when it might not, depending on format version) and lacked any explanation of format-version-specific encoding differences for dimensions and coordinates.

expectation.grounded: The documentation must include separate examples for Zarr V2 and Zarr V3 formats. The Zarr V2 example must demonstrate the _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS attribute and coordinates attributes visible via zarr-python. The Zarr V3 example must demonstrate the dimension_names field in metadata and the coordinates attribute from CF conventions. A 'Dimension Encoding in Zarr Formats' section must explain the V2/V3 differences. A 'Coordinate Encoding' section must explain CF conventions. A 'Compatibility and Reading' section must be reorganized for clarity.
expectation.conceptual: The Zarr encoding documentation should provide clear, format-version-specific examples showing what users will observe when accessing xarray-written Zarr stores using raw zarr-python. Users should be able to understand the relationship between dimension metadata, array dimension attributes, and coordinate attributes across Zarr format versions.

constraints.grounded: Documentation examples must produce output consistent with actual zarr-python behavior for both Zarr V2 and V3 formats. The _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS attribute must only be shown in the V2 context, and dimension_names metadata must only be shown in the V3 context. No runtime code changes are introduced.
constraints.conceptual: The documentation must not present ambiguous or format-agnostic examples that could mislead users about what attributes or metadata they will encounter. Each example must clearly indicate which Zarr format version it applies to.

behavior: Zarr V2 documentation example shows _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS and coordinates attributes when accessing arrays via zarr-python
Zarr V3 documentation example shows coordinates attribute and dimension_names in array metadata when accessing arrays via zarr-python

task_12.title: Fix to_netcdf compute=False failure with Dask Distributed
task_12.description: In xarray 2025.9.0, calling to_netcdf with compute=False and then executing the delayed computation via dask.compute() raises a BlockingIOError when using the Dask Distributed scheduler. Multiple workers attempt to open the same file concurrently, causing file-locking conflicts. This regression from 2025.8.0 is fixed by introducing a PickleableFileManager that correctly supports serialization for distributed task dispatch, allowing each worker to independently reopen the file without lock contention.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that calling Dataset.to_netcdf with compute=False and subsequently executing the delayed result via dask.compute() completes successfully when using the Dask Distributed scheduler. Prior to this fix, this workflow raised a BlockingIOError due to file-locking conflicts when distributed workers attempted to concurrently access the target file. This is a regression fix restoring behavior that worked in xarray 2025.8.0.

expectation.grounded: A new PickleableFileManager class (subclass of FileManager) must be used for delayed netCDF write operations. PickleableFileManager must support pickling via __getstate__/__setstate__, reopening the file on deserialization rather than relying on a global file cache. The manager must convert write mode ('w') to append mode ('a') upon reconstruction so that subsequent workers append to the already-created file rather than truncating it. The acquire() and acquire_context() methods must not require locking. When PickleableFileManager is closed, its __del__ method should warn via RuntimeWarning if the warn_for_unclosed_files option is enabled. An atexit handler must remove __del__ methods from both CachingFileManager and PickleableFileManager to prevent errors during interpreter shutdown.
expectation.conceptual: When a user calls to_netcdf with compute=False and later executes the delayed computation with Dask Distributed, the file manager wrapping the target netCDF file must be serializable so that distributed workers can independently open the file without global state or lock contention. Each worker should be able to write its assigned chunks without triggering file-locking errors. The delayed write workflow must produce the same output file as the immediate (compute=True) workflow.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not break the existing CachingFileManager or DummyFileManager behavior. The PickleableFileManager must not use global file caches or threading locks. The write-to-append mode conversion must only apply to the mode parameter during reconstruction after pickling, not during the initial open. The atexit cleanup of __del__ methods must cover both CachingFileManager and PickleableFileManager. The FileManager base class generic typing (FileManager[T_File]) must be preserved across all subclasses.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not regress existing to_netcdf behavior for synchronous writes (compute=True), local Dask scheduler usage, or any other file-backed storage workflows. File safety guarantees (proper close, resource cleanup, unclosed-file warnings) must be maintained. Serialization support must work transparently without requiring user-facing API changes.

behavior: PickleableFileManager opens the file eagerly in its constructor rather than lazily on first acquire
PickleableFileManager does not use locking for acquire, acquire_context, or close operations
When pickled, PickleableFileManager stores the opener callable, args, mode, and kwargs but omits the open file handle
When unpickled, PickleableFileManager calls its opener to reopen the file, converting 'w' mode to 'a' mode to avoid truncating the already-initialized file
If PickleableFileManager is garbage collected while still open, it closes the file and optionally emits a RuntimeWarning based on the warn_for_unclosed_files option
An atexit handler removes __del__ from both CachingFileManager and PickleableFileManager to avoid errors during interpreter shutdown
DummyFileManager gains generic type parameterization (FileManager[T_File]) and type annotations but its runtime behavior is unchanged
acceptance_criteria: When a Dataset with dask-backed arrays calls to_netcdf with compute=False using the netcdf4 engine, and the delayed result is executed via dask.compute() with a Dask Distributed client, the file is written successfully without BlockingIOError

When a Dataset with dask-backed arrays calls to_netcdf with compute=False using the h5netcdf engine, and the delayed result is executed via dask.compute() with a Dask Distributed client, the file is written successfully without BlockingIOError
When the delayed write task is serialized and sent to a Dask Distributed worker, the file manager is correctly pickled and unpickled, reopening the file in append mode on the worker
When to_netcdf is called with compute=True (the default), behavior is unchanged and files are written correctly
When to_netcdf with compute=False is executed with the default local Dask scheduler (not Distributed), the write completes successfully
When a PickleableFileManager is closed, calling acquire() raises a RuntimeError indicating the file is closed
When a PickleableFileManager is garbage collected without being explicitly closed, a RuntimeWarning is emitted if warn_for_unclosed_files is enabled

task_17.title: Enable full mypy type checking for all test files and fix scipy fallback import typing
task_17.description: All test files now have full mypy type checking enabled by removing the remaining exclusions for test_coding_times and test_dask from the mypy configuration. As part of fixing the resulting type errors, a guarded import of scipy.io.netcdf_file was added to the scipy backend module so that the optional-dependency fallback path satisfies the type checker. No user-facing runtime behavior changes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the xarray project enforces full mypy type checking (check_untyped_defs = true) across all test files, including test_coding_times and test_dask, and that all resulting type errors in both test and library code are resolved. Specifically, ensure that the scipy backend module's fallback import path for the optional scipy dependency is correctly typed so that mypy reports no errors when scipy is not installed.

expectation.grounded: The mypy configuration in pyproject.toml should no longer list xarray.tests.test_coding_times or xarray.tests.test_dask under the check_untyped_defs = false exclusion list. The xarray.backends.scipy_ module should define a module-level netcdf_file_base name via a try/except that imports scipy.io.netcdf_file when scipy is available and falls back to object when it is not, with appropriate type: ignore annotations. Running mypy with check_untyped_defs = true on the full test suite should produce no new errors.
expectation.conceptual: All test modules should pass strict mypy type checking without exclusions. The scipy backend module should cleanly handle the case where scipy is an optional dependency from a type-checking perspective, providing a valid fallback base reference when scipy is absent.

constraints.grounded: Removing the mypy exclusions must not introduce any new mypy errors in test_coding_times.py or test_dask.py. The fallback assignment for netcdf_file_base in xarray.backends.scipy_ must not alter runtime behavior when scipy is installed or when it is absent. Any type: ignore comments added must be narrowly scoped to specific error codes (e.g., assignment, misc) rather than blanket suppressions.
constraints.conceptual: Enabling stricter type checking must not break existing tests or change any runtime behavior. Type-ignore annotations should be minimal and precisely targeted rather than broad suppressions. The optional nature of the scipy dependency must be preserved.

When scipy is installed, the scipy backend module imports netcdf_file_base from scipy.io.netcdf_file and the backend functions identically to before
When scipy is not installed, the scipy backend module falls back to object for netcdf_file_base without raising ImportError at module import time

task_16.title: Refactor backends module to separate writers from readers
task_16.description: The backends module is restructured so that all data-writing functions are consolidated into a dedicated writers submodule, while the existing api submodule retains only read/open-related public API. The separate datatree I/O module is deleted and its contents merged into the new writers submodule. Additionally, the default netCDF write engine selection logic is rewritten to use the user-configurable engine order option and to support NCZarr mode detection. A new supports_groups class attribute is added to BackendEntrypoint so that engine guessing can filter backends by group-reading capability. The NetCDF4 backend's guess_can_open method now also handles bytes and memoryview inputs directly.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement:
Ensure that the xarray backends module cleanly separates data-writing concerns from data-reading concerns. Specifically:
- All write-oriented functions (to_netcdf, to_zarr, save_mfdataset, dump_to_store, and their supporting helpers) must be relocated out of the read-focused API module into a dedicated writers submodule.
- The standalone datatree I/O module must be eliminated, with its writer implementations merged into the same writers submodule.
- All public entry points (Dataset.to_netcdf, Dataset.to_zarr, DataArray.to_netcdf, DataArray.to_zarr, DataTree.to_netcdf, DataTree.to_zarr, xr.save_mfdataset) must continue to work identically from the user's perspective.
- The default write engine selection must honor the user-configurable netcdf_engine_order option from xarray.set_options and must detect NCZarr mode from path suffixes.
- BackendEntrypoint must expose a supports_groups class-level attribute so that engine guessing for group-aware operations (open_datatree, open_groups) can skip backends that lack group support.
- The NetCDF4 backend's engine-guessing probe must accept bytes and memoryview inputs in addition to file paths.

expectation.grounded: After the refactor: (1) The functions to_netcdf, to_zarr, save_mfdataset, dump_to_store, get_writable_netcdf_store, get_writable_zarr_store, and get_default_netcdf_write_engine must be importable from xarray.backends.writers. (2) xr.save_mfdataset must remain accessible as a top-level export from the xarray namespace. (3) Dataset.to_netcdf, Dataset.to_zarr, Dataset.dump_to_store, DataArray.to_netcdf, DataArray.to_zarr, DataTree.to_netcdf, and DataTree.to_zarr must internally import from xarray.backends.writers. (4) get_default_netcdf_write_engine must accept a path_or_file argument (str, IOBase, or None) and a format argument, must read the candidate order from OPTIONS['netcdf_engine_order'], must validate format against the set {NETCDF4, NETCDF4_CLASSIC, NETCDF3_64BIT, NETCDF3_CLASSIC}, and must force engine to netcdf4 when the path ends with '#mode=nczarr'. (5) When format is not 'NETCDF4', h5netcdf must be excluded from write engine candidates; when format is not 'NETCDF3_64BIT' or 'NETCDF3_CLASSIC', scipy must be excluded. (6) When path_or_file is an IOBase instance, netcdf4 must be excluded from write engine candidates. (7) BackendEntrypoint must define supports_groups as a ClassVar[bool] defaulting to False. NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint and H5netcdfBackendEntrypoint must set supports_groups = True. (8) guess_engine must accept a must_support_groups boolean parameter and, when True, skip backends where supports_groups is False and raise a specific error if no group-supporting backend is found. (9) NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open must handle bytes and memoryview by reading the first 8 bytes directly. (10) The xarray.core.datatree_io module must no longer exist; the type aliases T_DataTreeNetcdfEngine and T_DataTreeNetcdfTypes must be defined in xarray.backends.writers.
expectation.conceptual: All write-path functions are consolidated under a single writers submodule while all public user-facing APIs (Dataset.to_netcdf, Dataset.to_zarr, DataArray.to_netcdf, DataArray.to_zarr, DataTree.to_netcdf, DataTree.to_zarr, xr.save_mfdataset) remain fully functional with identical signatures and behavior. Default write engine selection respects the user-configurable engine order setting and properly handles NCZarr paths. Backend entrypoints declare whether they support group operations, allowing engine guessing to filter appropriately when opening hierarchical data. The NetCDF4 backend can now probe bytes and memoryview objects directly when guessing whether it can open a given input.

constraints.grounded: All existing public API call signatures on Dataset, DataArray, DataTree, and the xr namespace for writing data must remain unchanged. The overloaded type signatures of to_netcdf and to_zarr must be preserved. The WRITEABLE_STORES mapping must map T_NetcdfEngine keys to the same backend store open callables (NetCDF4DataStore.open, ScipyDataStore, H5NetCDFStore.open). BackendEntrypoint subclasses that do not explicitly set supports_groups must default to False (non-breaking for third-party backends). The guess_engine function's must_support_groups parameter must default to False so that existing callers are unaffected. The autoclose logic extracted into _get_netcdf_autoclose must still raise NotImplementedError for scipy with distributed or multiprocessing schedulers.
constraints.conceptual: No user-facing API signatures may change. Third-party backend entrypoints must not break due to the new supports_groups attribute. The refactoring must not alter the observable behavior of any write operation. The engine selection order must remain user-configurable. Error messages for unrecognized engines, invalid formats, and missing backend libraries must remain informative.
